name: Tessera Industries Phantom Blade PB-1 'Ghost Knife'
description: A combat knife with a blade forged from Tessera's proprietary metamaterial composite that absorbs electromagnetic radiation across the visible and near-infrared spectrum, rendering it functionally invisible to optical and thermal sensors. The blade appears as a void — a knife-shaped absence of light that the eye struggles to track. The metamaterial construction also gives the blade unusual physical properties: it is extremely hard but brittle, capable of penetrating body armor through sheer material hardness but prone to shattering if used to pry or lever. Each blade is individually manufactured and serial-coded, making them traceable — which has not stopped them from becoming prestige assassination tools.
specifications:
blade length: 18 cm
blade material: Tessera EM-absorbing metamaterial composite
hardness: Exceeds tungsten carbide
optical signature: Absorbs 99.7% of visible and near-IR light
thermal signature: Undetectable to standard thermal imaging
weight: 0.15 kg
fragility: Shatters under lateral stress exceeding 40 Nm
story_hooks: A Ghost Knife was recovered from a crime scene with its serial code intact — tracing the sale leads to a Tessera executive who reported it stolen six months ago, or claims to have.

A forger is selling counterfeit Ghost Knives made from conventional metamaterial that degrades after weeks — buyers are finding their 'invisible' blades becoming visible at the worst possible moments.
related_entities: Kessler Kinetics VelocityFrame MkIV Sprint Leg

physical_description.visual_profile: A knife-shaped void. The blade appears as an absence of light—a negative space that creates an optical illusion of non-existence. The eye struggles to track it. Only the handle and crossguard register clearly; the blade itself seems to absorb all photons, creating a haunting silhouette that contradicts the weight in your hand.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length 32 cm (blade 18 cm, handle 14 cm). Blade width 4.2 cm at widest point. Thickness 0.8 cm. Profile suggests a tanto or modified bowie—slightly curved, aggressive geometry.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light at 150 grams—almost insubstantial until you feel the dense, brittle composite in your palm. The weight sits forward in the blade. Feels like holding concentrated absence.
physical_description.primary_material: Tessera proprietary EM-absorbing metamaterial composite (blade). Likely tungsten-matrix substrate. Handle appears to be reinforced polymer or composite resin.
physical_description.finish: The blade has no finish—or rather, all finishes are consumed by it. Zero reflectivity. Matte beyond matte. The handle shows brushed satin texture, possibly anodized aluminum or hard polymer, providing stark contrast.
physical_description.color_scheme: The blade reads as absolute black or deep void-gray depending on ambient light—it shifts between non-colors. Handle is matte gunmetal gray or charcoal with subtle metallic undertones. Crossguard likely matches handle in darker gray.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer or wrapped composte—slightly aggressive texture for retention. Designed for wet/augmented hands. Subtle ribbing or knurling visible in product photography.
distinctive_features: Blade appears as knife-shaped void—optical absorption creates visual paradox
Crossguard asymmetrical, designed for close-quarters manipulation
No visible edge—the absence of light makes cutting geometry invisible
Subtle serial etchings on handle (Tessera traceability coding)
Microfractures visible on blade surface under close inspection—hints of brittleness
Heat vents or stress-relief patterns etched into blade near crossguard
Handle features small indentation for thumb placement—aggressive ergonomics
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Tessera Industries logo (geometric Φ-derived symbol) stamped on pommel. Serial code laser-etched on handle near crossguard. Product designation 'PB-1' appears as faint marking on crossguard—intentionally subdued.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine in catalogue photos. In field use, shows stress fractures and micro-damage along blade edges. Some units appear chipped or partially shattered from lateral impacts. Handles show wear from repeated use and environmental exposure.
